I5.quote: In this study, we compressed hydrogen up to 70 MPa in a non-mechanical device based on cyclic, thermally driven, hydrogen adsorption/desorption on activated carbon (AC).

notes: Experimental and numerical study of a thermally driven adsorption-desorption H2 compressor filled with MSC-30 or MSP20X activated carbon (0.5 L tank, charged at 77 K and 4-8 MPa, heated to 298-353 K). Not theoretical_only (experimental pressure, temperature and flow data are reported) and not electrochemical, so the I1 failure is coded no_conditions_stated. Passages considered and rejected for I1: (a) 'In our previous study [7], we showed that the lower hydrogen uptake on MSP20X, i.e., 4.8 wt%' (main, p. 11, Section 4.4) is quoted from other work; (b) 'the ratio of compressed hydrogen mass to tank volume was equal to 0.951 g L-1' (main, p. 11, Section 4.5) is the compressed (delivered) hydrogen per tank volume of the system, not an amount taken up by the sorbent at a stated T and P; (c) Table 2 'Maximum hydrogen adsorbed/mol kg-1 xm 72.46 [7]' is an MDA fit parameter from ref. [7]; (d) Fig. 7a adsorbed-phase density is from numerical simulation. Charging was until 'the FT 1 flowmeter did not record any incoming flow' (Section 2.3) but no integrated charge amount is given. If I1 were judged met, Table 1 gives BET areas (MSC-30 3305, MSP20X 2363 m2 g-1, from ref. [7]) for the measured samples. Not a review; record is_retracted false and no retraction statement in the PDF. No supplementary files were provided.
